newsitem.title: USA: FDA clears latest in new wave of schizophrenia drugs.
newsitem.headline: FDA clears latest in new wave of schizophrenia drugs.

text.p: The latest in a wave of new drugs to treat schizophrenia more effectively and with fewer side effects was approved Tuesday by the Food and Drug Administration.
Zyprexa, made by Indianapolis-based Eli Lilly & Co., is expected to hit the market in a few days.
Along with similar drugs recently released and still to come from several companies over the next year or so, Zyprexa offers schizophrenics new options, researchers said.
Schizophrenia affects about 1 percent of the world population. Victims typically suffer from hallucinations, delusions and difficulty telling fantasy from reality.
Most cannot work and must be supported by others. A third of U.S. psychiatric hospital beds hold schizophrenics.

"Schizophrenia patients account for a significant number of all beds in U.S. psychiatric hospitals. This represents a tremendous cost, which is often borne by public sources, such as state and federal governments," said Dr. Gary Tollefson, vice president of Lilly Research Laboratories.
Zyprexa is one of a class of innovative compounds called atypical antipsychotics that treat schizophrenia's symptoms better than older drugs and with fewer side-effects.

The new drugs cost more -- about $6.48 per tablet for Zyprexa -- than older treatments, such as generic haloperidol, which costs less than 50 cents per day for treatment. But Lilly maintained that Zyprexa compensates for its higher cost by keeping patients out of the hospital and functioning in society.
